core_obligations: Prove weak convergence with fixed marginals strengthens to uniform CDF convergence even at marginal atoms.
Characterize this metric through all products of bounded monotone test functions, not only continuous test functions.
Derive almost-sure convergence of conditional expectations from monotonicity plus integral convergence.
Combine that pointwise convergence with a uniform bound on the varying product test function to prove continuity of two-plan concatenation, then iterate.

proof_roadmap.step: Use fixed marginal mass bounds at rectangle boundaries, then a finite grid separating large atoms, to establish the uniform CDF metric.
Layer-cake decomposition represents monotone products as mixtures of rectangle indicators.
A limsup/liminf contradiction on a small interval yields almost-sure convergence of monotone conditional expectations.
Split the varying-plan/varying-function integral difference: uniform metric controls one part and dominated convergence controls the other. Iterate across a finite chain.

difficulty_reason: The Markov concatenation operation is not weakly continuous in general. Even after ordinary measure-theory prerequisites, this proof has to exploit fixed marginals to control rectangle boundaries at atoms, strengthen weak convergence to uniform monotone-product tests, and combine that control with almost-sure monotone conditional-kernel limits. That synthesis is the nonroutine substance; the item is not a direct application of dominated convergence. H2 is a selector judgment pending independent examination of the disclosed source notation.
